text:
Anya: Heads-up: I uploaded a new variant of the autoscale controls. Goal: make Min/Max + Burst + Pool selection fit in a compact right rail while keeping clarity. Share quick thoughts. Link in PR. Priya: Love that you squeezed it. Two immediate concerns: 1) burst state confusion (users think burst=permanent) and 2) pool dropdown with 40 pools will be terrible. Marco: Agreed on pool size. Recommend modal with search + grouping by region. Add tiny badges (GPU type, cost tier) on each row. Jen: Copy suggestion: change "Burst" to "Burst (temporary)" and add hover tooltip: "Temporary extra instances that scale down automatically; billed while active." Short and explicit. Kevin: A11y: for a compact dual-stepper (Min/Max) ensure each stepper has aria-labels: aria-label="Min instances" and aria-label="Max instances". Include aria-live region that announces changes: e.g.,
Max set to 12, estimated +2.1% cost
. Anya: UX question: show cost delta inline next to the number or only in the cost preview panel? Priya: Inline is better. Users experiment with numbers quickly and need instant feedback. Make it subtle: 12 (+2.1%). Also allow toggling units (tokens/hr vs $/hr) in the cost preview modal. Marco: Implementation note: we can compute delta client-side using current workload profile. We'll need an events contract: autoscale.adjust and autoscale.preview for telemetry. Kevin: Pool modal needs keyboard filter focus on open, role=dialog, and Escape to close. Each pool row should be a button with aria-pressed for selection. For multi-column mobile view, ensure the modal is full screen. UX-research: We tested 6 users with a similar compact rail. 4/6 expected Max to be primary; they tried to drag the Max slider when Min was focused. Recommendation: visually emphasize Max (bolder label) and keep Min lighter. Jen: Microcopy for SLO slider: "SLO target (%): Higher = more provisioned capacity, lower failure risk. Lower = cost savings." Add short inline guardrail text under 60%: "Warning: <60% may increase throttled requests" in orange. Anya: Guardrails: should setting SLO <50 be allowed? We have backend limit of 30 but UX could warn strongly. Marco: Engine constraints: backend enforces min_slo=30. UX should prevent values <30 and explain with tooltip. Also show recommended SLO for common workloads (in a small dropdown: latency-sensitive, throughput, cost-optimized). Priya: For burst, default to off in Dedicated pools, default on for Hosted for PLG discoverability. Make default clearly shown and add contextual help link to docs. Kevin: For the compact layout, keyboard order should be: Pool picker -> SLO slider -> Max stepper -> Min stepper -> Burst toggle -> Save. That keeps primary actions first. Ensure focus outlines match high-contrast themes. Jen: Also propose a tiny "why this matters" link that opens a short explainer modal (1-2 bullets) about how Min/Max/Burst interact. Good for support triage. Anya: @Marco can you add the telemetry event names in the PR? @Kevin can you paste a short checklist for aria attributes to attach to the design? @UX-research can you share the 2 quotes from the user tests? Marco: Will add events: autoscale.open_panel, autoscale.change_min, autoscale.change_max, autoscale.toggle_burst, autoscale.select_pool, autoscale.set_slo. Each event should include {user_id, session_id, prev_value, new_value, source_ui}. Kevin: Checklist (short): 1) role=dialog for pool modal, 2) focus trap on open, 3) aria-labels for steppers and slider, 4) aria-live announcer for value changes, 5) aria-pressed on pool rows, 6) keyboard order validated, 7) visible focus styles high-contrast. I'll paste a code snippet in the PR. Jen: I'll land microcopy PR after Marco adds events. Tiny tooltip text samples in the branch. deploy-bot: Design feedback thread created 11802501120 024 (DR-3497). Reviewers: @product-team. Link: https://jira/redwood/DR-3497 Anya: Great. If no objections I'll merge after Marco/Kevin updates. Thanks all!
